key_insight: AISPA proposes a user-centric way to audit hidden system prompts in AI applications, helping reveal how these prompts shape model behavior. It aims to close the transparency gap between developers, users, and regulators.
problem_solved: Commercial AI systems often rely on undisclosed system prompts that strongly influence outputs, making it difficult to verify safety, accountability, and policy compliance.
method: Defines Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance (AISPA) as a structured auditing framework for system prompts.
Focuses on user-centric inspection of prompt behavior and its downstream effects in real AI applications.
Systematically checks whether prompt instructions align with expected policies, safety goals, and user-facing behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, AISPA offers a practical path toward better transparency, governance, and trust in deployed LLM products. It can help teams evaluate hidden prompt risks before they cause safety, compliance, or reliability issues.
visual_elements: A layered architecture diagram showing user, application, system prompt, and model interaction.
A flowchart of the AISPA auditing process from prompt discovery to evaluation results.
A comparison chart contrasting disclosed vs. undisclosed system prompts and their risks.
An icon-based trust/governance panel highlighting transparency, safety, and accountability.
paper_title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
paper_authors: Xiangning Lin, Shenzhe Zhu, Shu Yang, Zhenyu Zhang, Haoqian Zhang
